transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-09
Start: 16:00 UTC | Duration: ~45m
Attendees: Marcus Lang (Redwood AE), Priya Kapoor (Redwood SE), Jesse Park (Redwood Solutions Eng); Eleni Ortiz (Halcyon Head of Security), Derek Shaw (CTO), Marta Ruiz (Data Privacy Lead), Omar Li (Platform Eng)

Summary:
Quick technical review focused on how Redwood handles ephemeral prompts, encryption and KMS integration, RBAC/SSO, audit logs, and the explicit no-training guarantee for customer content. Agreed to run a short pilot for ephemeral retention policy and to share SOC2 artifacts and KMS integration examples.

Topics covered:
- Prompt retention / ephemeral mode / no-training opt outs
- Encryption in transit and at rest; BYOK / KMS integration options
- RBAC, SSO (SAML/Okta), service accounts and least privilege
- Audit logging, retention windows, SIEM integration (Splunk/Sumo/Datadog)
- Data residency & private deployment options for air-gapped or EU-only workloads

Action items (recap here and in metadata): see action_items field.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Marcus: Hey everyone, thanks for carving time today, I'll hand to Priya to kick off the technical bit, but quick intro — I'm Marcus, AE, Priya is our SE — we do a lot of these security deep dives so feel free to interrupt.
[00:28] Priya: Hi all. Quick agenda: ephemeral prompts and retention, KMS/BYOK options, RBAC/SSO, audit logs, and then Q&A. We'll surface any gotchas and how we map to SOC 2 controls.
[01:05] Eleni: Thanks. Big things for us: we need firm statements on whether customer prompts or generated content can ever be used to improve models. Also KMS integration for keys with HSM is a blocker for some of our regulators.
[01:40] Priya: Understood. To be clear up front — Redwood's hosted offering does not use customer prompts or outputs to train open models by default. We have an explicit policy: customer data is not part of our training corp unless the customer signs a separate opt-in. That means no signal from your prompts flow into model training.
[02:12] Derek: So like, you're not aggregating prompt data for next-model training? Just confirming.
[02:20] Marcus: Correct. No training. Also we can offer dedicated or private deployments if you want physical isolation.
[03:05] Marta: Can you point to the contractual language? We need something we can hand to legal that is explicit — "no training on customer data" with exceptions noted.
[03:28] Marcus: Yes, we'll send a short clause and reference to the privacy whitepaper and the SOC 2 report. I'll add that to the notes.
[04:05] Priya: Moving to retention — we support ephemeral prompt retention policies. You can set per-route retention to zero after X seconds or configure a strict ephemeral mode where prompts aren't persisted beyond transit, aside from transient KV cache for active sessions. Note: the KV cache — sometimes speech-to-text writes it as K-V cash — it's just an in-memory cache for ongoing context and it can be disabled.
[04:56] Omar: That KV cache, is that flushed on session end and never written to disk?
[05:02] Priya: Correct, by default it's in-RAM on the serving instance and not persisted to disk, and with ephemeral mode we make sure it's cleared post-session. For Dedicated and Private setups we can also enforce memory-only policies via config.
[05:40] Eleni: Good. How about logs — we need immutable audit trails for all admin actions and API keys, ideally 365 days. Does Redwood provide that out of the box?
[06:00] Jesse: We stream audit logs to your tenant's log sink — S3, GCS, or direct SIEM integration. Logs include API key usage, token expends, model switch events, policy changes, and RBAC changes. Retention is configurable; default is 90, we can do 365 for enterprise.
[06:30] Derek: Are logs tamper-evident or signed?
[06:36] Jesse: We support log signing for audit chains and append-only storage via object versioning and immutability windows, and we can provide signed checksums on request.
[07:10] Marta: KMS — we need BYOK and HSM-backed keys. Can you walk through an integration pattern?
[07:22] Priya: Sure. Two main patterns: customer-managed KMS where keys are in your cloud KMS (Google Cloud KMS, AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault) and Redwood encrypts model cache and persistent artifacts with a data key wrapped by your KMS master key; second is an HSM option for private/offline deployments. With hosted, we do envelope encryption, and you hold the root key. We can rotate keys per your schedule.
[08:05] Eleni: If keys are in our KMS, can Redwood decrypt without us handing over the key? How is access gated?
[08:18] Priya: Access is gated by ephemeral service accounts with least privilege. For hosted we never ask you to hand over root keys; we request Decrypt permissions on wrapped data keys so we can run inference, but key usage can be logged in your KMS audit logs. For Private deployments where you run the control plane, you keep all keys locally.
[08:55] Omar: Any latency impact with envelope decryption per request?
[09:00] Jesse: Minor, we cache decrypted data keys in memory for a short TTL to avoid KMS roundtrips on every token. Costs and latency are considered in our recommendations; we'll include perf numbers in the KMS doc.
[09:45] Derek: SSO and RBAC — we use Okta. Need SCIM provisioning and fine-grained roles.
[09:53] Priya: We support SAML 2.0 and SCIM for user provisioning, role mappings, and attribute-based access control. Roles: Admin, Dev, Billing, ReadOnly, and custom roles. We can integrate enterprise SSO and map groups to Redwood roles.
[10:30] Marta: Can we enforce session timeout and MFA at least?
[10:35] Priya: Yes, session timeouts are enforced by the IdP and we can require MFA via SAML assertions.
[11:10] Eleni: For compliance, we need a SOC 2 Type II report and an ISO 27001 cert. Are those available?
[11:20] Marcus: We have SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001, yes — we'll share the latest reports under an NDA if needed. Also we publish a security whitepaper that maps controls to our architecture.
[11:58] Marta: Great. Can you outline which SOC 2 CC controls map to retention and training assurances?
[12:10] Priya: We'll send a mapping doc; short answer: the controls around change management, data handling, and confidentiality are covered and we call out the contract/opt-in for training on customer content.
[13:02] Derek: About model fallbacks — if a high-throughput event happens, will the system route to cheaper models and could that affect PII handling?
[13:15] Jesse: Routing policy is configurable. Default is to maintain class-of-service separation. You can pin routes to models, and fallbacks will only use variants approved for your tenant. We won't silently route sensitive routes to unmanaged endpoints.
[14:00] Eleni: For data residency — our EU regulator wants data never leave the EU. Can you commit to EU-only processing?
[14:12] Marcus: Yes, we can pin processing to EU regions in Hosted, or run a Private deployment in your region. We'll provide an architecture sketch.
[15:02] Omar: Network connectivity: for the KMS flow and audit logs, we'll want VPC peering and minimal public egress. Is that supported?
[15:14] Priya: Yes — VPC peering and private networking is supported on Dedicated and Private, and Hosted can be configured with private endpoints. We'll provide a VPC checklist.
[16:00] Marta: One concern: the phrase "not used to train our models" — sometimes sales language is too fuzzy for auditors. We need explicit contractual text and technical guarantees.
[16:22] Marcus: Understood. We'll provide exact contract wording, an engineering note describing data flows, and the SOC 2 mapping.
[17:00] Derek: For the pilot, how would ephemeral retention be enforced?
[17:10] Priya: We can deploy a per-route policy for the pilot: incoming prompt stored transiently only in RAM for X minutes, no disk writes, KV cache disabled, and logs redacted for content. We'll also set log retention and ensure no content snapshots are stored.
[18:05] Eleni: If we need additional scrubbing, do you offer PII redaction pre-ingest?
[18:12] Priya: We have a pre-processing pipeline you can plug in to scrub or pseudonymize PII before it hits the runtime; alternatively customers route inputs through their own scrubbing proxy.
[19:00] Marta: About regulatory audits: can auditors get read-only access to logs or an evidence package?
[19:12] Jesse: Yes. We can produce an evidence bundle (redacted as necessary) and provide read-only access to audit logs for a bounded time window.
[20:00] (short pause; cross-talk)
[21:10] Eleni: On encryption at rest, can you confirm which artifacts are encrypted? Model weights, KV cache, disk image snapshots?
[21:22] Priya: Model weights are encrypted at rest; ephemeral KV cache is memory-only in ephemeral mode; disk snapshots are encrypted and wrapped with customer-managed keys when BYOK is enabled.
[22:05] Derek: Is there an automated key-rotation mechanism that won't disrupt ongoing sessions?
[22:12] Jesse: Yes — we do key rotation with double-wrap technique and staged rollout; decrypted data keys are cached briefly so rotation is transparent for active sessions.
[23:00] Marta: Regarding "no training" — will there be logs proving no training events occurred?
[23:12] Marcus: We can supply logs showing ingestion pipelines and confirm there's no data flow into training buckets. For audits, we'll show pipeline configs and that training corpuses are segregated.
[24:00] Marta: Any third-party subprocessors? We need a list.
[24:08] Marcus: We'll share an updated subprocessors list in the SOC 2 artifact packet.
[25:00] Omar: Performance question — if we disable KV cache and enforce ephemeral mode, what's the latency impact?
[25:12] Jesse: Depends on model and sequence lengths; rough ballpark 10–25% higher token latency for small models, might be 5–10% for larger context-optimized models. We'll provide a short benchmark in the pilot.
[26:40] Eleni: Ok good. Can we get a short written summary for our security steering committee?
[26:50] Marcus: Yes — we'll prepare a 1–page summary, include contract language, SOC 2 references, and the pilot plan.
[27:30] Derek: Also want to know about incident response and SLAs for data breaches.
[27:38] Priya: We have an incident response playbook, breach notification timelines aligned with regulatory requirements, and enterprise customers can opt into faster notification SLAs.
[28:20] Marta: Does Redwood support data subject access request handling or will customers need to handle that?
[28:30] Jesse: We provide tooling and logs to assist. For things like deletion requests, we support programmatic deletion endpoints and will help coordinate if you need us to act on behalf of the customer subject to contract.
[29:05] (brief back-and-forth about scheduling the pilot)
[30:00] Marcus: Proposed pilot: 2 weeks ephemeral mode on a subset of routes, KMS BYOK via AWS KMS, EU-region processing. Pilot runbook and checklist we'll share.
[30:25] Eleni: That sounds fine. We'll confirm infra windows.
[31:10] Priya: I'll share runnable terraform snippets for the KMS integration and a small perf matrix for expected latency.
[31:40] Marta: Also request: a clause in the master services agreement explicitly prohibiting model training without opt-in plus a mechanism to demonstrate compliance.
[31:52] Marcus: Noted — we'll include that clause and an evidence checklist.
[33:00] Derek: Any mention of competitors? We're evaluating Anthropic for safety controls and OpenAI for capabilities. What's Redwood's differentiator here?
[33:12] Marcus: Our differentiator is production-grade controls and the ability to run private deployments with strong KMS/HSM support plus the explicit, contract-backed no-training position.
[34:05] Omar: Minor nit: sometimes docs refer to "Redwood private" or "redwood privat" in transcriptions — which doc is canonical?
[34:12] Priya: We'll share canonical architecture diagrams in the packet.
[35:10] (Questions from Halcyon about cost of private deployment vs hosted)
[36:00] Marcus: We'll include pricing ranges for hosted with 365-day log retention and for a small dedicated pool; exact quotes after scoping.
[37:20] Marta: Last technical question: can you do per-tenant model pinning so we never fall back to externally trained variants?
[37:30] Priya: Yes; model pinning per route is standard. We'll show how to lock to a family or exact version.
[38:12] Eleni: Ok thanks. Anything else?
[38:20] Jesse: Quick note: for the pilot we'll need an SRE contact and VPC admin to set up peering; Omar volunteered earlier.
[38:35] Omar: Yep, we'll coordinate.
[39:05] Marcus: Great. Recap of next steps in chat: SOC 2 artifacts, KMS doc, pilot runbook, contract clause.
[39:30] Marta: Sounds good. We'll review and get back with windows for the pilot.
[40:10] (wrap-up and small social sign off)
[44:30] End meeting.

References shared during call: SOC 2 summary (link - sent post-call), Redwood KMS integration notes (to be shared), Pilot runbook (to be shared).

Notes on transcript quality: medium - a few proper nouns and technical terms may be mis-transcribed (K-V cash, redwood privat), speaker overlaps occasionally attributed to the wrong label.
